This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chicago O'Hare Intl Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kord

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent northeasterly flow behind a recent frontal passage has suppressed maximum temperatures across the Chicago area on September 5, 2026, producing the dominant market-implied probability of 80–81 °F.** Official National Weather Service guidance and real-time observations from O’Hare and lakefront stations show afternoon readings holding in the mid-to-upper 70s near the water and low-to-mid 80s a few miles inland under mostly cloudy skies and 10–15 mph northeast winds. This represents a sharp cooldown from the prior four days’ 91–96 °F readings, consistent with the arrival of cooler, more stable air and reduced solar heating. Model consensus has remained tightly clustered around this range throughout the day, giving traders high confidence in the 80–81 °F bin. Only an unexpected rapid clearing of clouds combined with stronger boundary-layer mixing could push readings into the low 80s or above, an outcome assigned just 3.5 % combined probability.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread showers, and high humidity from a low-pressure system are capping daytime heating in Taipei, with Central Weather Administration forecasts and global models converging on a 26–29°C range for September 6. Heavy rain and overcast skies reduce incoming solar radiation while evaporation and cloud radiative effects further moderate surface temperatures, making 27°C and 28°C the most probable peaks according to the latest model runs. Trader consensus at 37% for 27°C and 31% for 28°C reflects this narrow band amid minor differences in model timing of heaviest precipitation; lower probabilities for 29°C or above acknowledge the slim chance of partial clearing allowing brief additional warming before renewed showers. Updated CWA guidance and next model cycle will refine resolution ahead of the daily maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest forecasts from models including GFS and local guidance indicate clear skies and light southerly to southeasterly winds over Cape Town on September 6, supporting daytime heating to a maximum in the mid-20s Celsius under stable high-pressure conditions typical of early spring. Trader consensus clusters tightly on 26°C or 27°C because ensemble spreads show minor differences in peak insolation timing, boundary-layer mixing, and coastal sea-breeze onset that can shift the observed high by 1–2°C. Official South African Weather Service outlooks describe “warm to hot” conditions across the western interior with very high UV, consistent with historical September maxima near 24–26°C at Cape Town International, while any late-day onshore flow or slight model cooling could cap readings at 25°C. Updated runs and real-time observations through the morning will likely narrow the narrow probability gap between the two leading outcomes.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Dallas Love Field Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kdal

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models from the National Weather Service and private providers show Dallas under persistent high pressure on September 6, 2026, with mostly sunny skies, light southeast winds, and afternoon highs expected in the upper 90s to low 100s.** Official guidance points to a peak near 98–101°F, with heat indices exceeding 105°F due to elevated dew points. The near-even split between the 98–99°F and 100–101°F market bins reflects small differences across model runs in timing of maximum heating, boundary-layer mixing, and any thin afternoon cloud debris. This late-summer pattern follows several consecutive days above 98°F, consistent with above-normal temperatures for early September when the long-term average high is about 92.5°F. Updated model guidance and any last-minute observational shifts will determine which bin resolves.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**A cold front advancing across Southeast Brazil is the dominant driver pushing trader consensus toward 15–16°C as the most probable high for São Paulo on September 6.** Official guidance from INMET and consensus from global models (including Yr and Met Office) indicate the front will deliver persistent cloud cover, southeasterly winds, and widespread rain or showers, sharply limiting daytime warming after a milder September 5. This setup favors maximum temperatures clustered around 14–16°C, with 15°C and 16°C holding the highest implied probabilities because model runs show only modest differences in frontal timing and boundary-layer mixing.

Key scientific factors differentiating the narrow 15–17°C band include the precise strength and speed of the post-frontal high-pressure ridge, which controls how quickly drier air arrives, the depth of low-level cloud suppressing solar heating, and local effects near the official observation site (typically Congonhas or INMET stations). Stronger southeasterly flow and heavier rain favor the lower end (14–15°C), while any earlier clearing or weaker winds could allow brief warming toward 17°C. Historical September averages near 23°C highlight how anomalous this event is, and traders are weighting the latest model consensus heavily given the short time to resolution. New forecast updates or radar trends on frontal position over the next 12–24 hours remain the primary variables that could shift probabilities within this tight range.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent short-range forecasts from ECMWF, GFS, and local models show a southerly flow advecting warmer air into the Netherlands, supporting a daytime maximum in Amsterdam on September 7 likely between 24–27 °C.** 

Model consensus points to partly cloudy conditions with peaks around midday to mid-afternoon, though differences in cloud timing, wind speed, and boundary-layer mixing create a narrow range of outcomes. This uncertainty, combined with above-normal early-September climatology (typical highs near 20–22 °C), explains the tight market split favoring 25 °C (40.5 %) and 26 °C (32.5 %). Updated ensemble runs and KNMI guidance ahead of resolution will be the key catalysts for any shift in trader-implied probabilities.

Thunderstorm development—driven by diurnal heating and residual monsoon moisture—tends to cap afternoon temperatures through increased cloud cover and evaporative cooling, reducing the likelihood of 36°C+ readings that would require clearer skies and stronger insolation. Short-range model runs and recent observations of persistent haze (which can suppress or enhance surface heating depending on aerosol loading) reinforce the narrow 33–35°C band as the most probable outcome, explaining why traders have concentrated capital on these three resolutions ahead of the September 7 verification window.

This represents a substantial departure from seasonal norms near 25°C. Model consensus from sources including Met Office and local agencies points to limited daytime heating due to overcast skies and modest winds, keeping peaks tightly clustered between 12–15°C. Minor differences among leading outcomes hinge on exact frontal timing, precipitation intensity, and boundary-layer mixing, with fresh model runs and INMET updates expected to refine the peak before resolution. Trader positioning reflects this narrow scientific uncertainty range.
